newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares recoup some losses in early bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares recoup some losses in early bourse.

text.p: A rebound on Wall Street overnight boosted sentiment in the German share market in early bourse trade, calmed dealers' nerves a little and saw the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips advance early on.
The DAX index was up 17.89 points, or 0.54 percent, at 3,313.82 points early on, just off early an session high of 3,316.73 points.

"There is still a lot of caution about, but I expect support and I expect we will recover some losses here in Frankfurt today. The index should settle around 3,300 points over the day," a Frankfurt trader said.
Shares in chemical giant BASF pushed to 61.90 marks in early bourse, a rise of 90 pfennigs or nearly 1.5 percent.
Dealers said the market was enthusiastic about the group's 1996 earnings per share (EPS), while the rest of the figures announced earlier were generally in line with expectations.
"The outlook was good. It was cautious, but then we've come to expect that from BASF," a Frankfurt trader.
Positive sentiment on the chemical sector helped lift other stocks. Bayer AG was up 1.84 percent at 68.95 marks, while Hoechst AG was up 1.65 pfennigs, nearly two and a half percent, at 65.75 marks.
Dealers expected to see some bargain-hunting over the course of bourse trade.
"But everyone is really just breathing a sigh of relief," a Frankfurt trader said.
